channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: UN Allocates $18 Million in Emergency Aid for Afghanistan
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has approved $18 million in emergency aid for Afghanistan, set to benefit over 824,000 vulnerable individuals. Funding from the UN Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) will support seven projects in food security, agriculture, health, and other critical areas.

item.title: Jordan and Iraq to Ban Telegram Over Security and Content Concerns
item.description: Jordan and Iraq have announced plans to ban the messaging app Telegram, citing national security concerns. The measures aim to prevent the spread of illegal and extremist content and compel Telegram to review content related to the countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Saida Mirziyoyeva Discusses Visa Facilitation with Canadian Ambassador
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, met with Canada's Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Christopher Dagan. They discussed facilitating visa procedures and expanding trade, investment, and business ties between the two countries.

item.title: Five Uzbek Schoolchildren Involved in Fatal Car Crash, One Dies
item.description: Five eighth-grade students were involved in a car accident on a road outside a village in Toyloq district, Samarqand region. One student died from injuries sustained in the crash. The driver, also a student, reportedly hit a tree. An investigation is underway, and the incident highlights a prevalent issue of underage driving in Uzbekistan.

item.title: One-Year-Old Dies of Measles in Kazakhstan's Atyrau Region
item.description: A one-year-old child has died from measles in the Atyrau region of Kazakhstan. The child was airlifted to a regional infectious diseases hospital in critical condition, suffering from bilateral pneumonia and respiratory and cardiac failure. Doctors noted the child had a congenital heart defect and parents had refused vaccination.

item.title: Two Schoolboys Suspected of Abusing Child in Kazakhstan's Kostanay Region
item.description: In Kazakhstan's Kostanay region, two sixth-grade students are suspected of sexually abusing a 10-year-old boy in a school restroom. The police have opened a criminal case. The 'NeMolchiKZ' foundation reported the incident, stating the alleged perpetrators were 11 and 12 years old. The regional ombudsman for children's rights is monitoring the situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Hosts Military Drone Challenge for State Agencies
item.description: A Military Drone Challenge tournament was held at the 'Maylan' field training center of the State Security Service of Kazakhstan. The competition aimed to improve skills in using and countering unmanned aerial systems. Teams from various Kazakh state bodies participated, with the State Security Service team securing first place.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Population Grew by Nearly 10 Million in 16 Years
item.description: Uzbekistan's permanent population has increased by almost 10 million people over the past 16 years. According to the Statistics Committee, the population grew from 29.2 million in early 2010 to 39 million by early 2026. The country surpassed 30 million residents in 2012 and has seen consistent demographic growth since.

item.title: Uzbekistan Leads CIS in Unemployment Rate Reduction Over Five Years
item.description: Uzbekistan has shown the most significant reduction in unemployment among CIS countries over the past five years, decreasing by over half from 10.5% in 2020 to 4.8% by the end of 2025. Kyrgyzstan also saw a notable decrease. Overall, unemployment in the CIS region fell from 3.4% to 3.1% between 2024 and 2025.

item.title: Kazakhstan Security Forces Compete in Drone Operations Challenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's security forces participated in the MILITARY DRONE CHALLENGE, a competition testing their skills in operating drones and countering unmanned aerial systems. Held at the 'Maylan' training ground, teams from various state bodies executed tasks simulating real-world scenarios. The State Security Service of Kazakhstan secured first place.

item.title: Oman's Voltamp Energy to Invest $350 Million in Uzbekistan Solar Power Plant
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have signed a joint development agreement for a 500 MW solar photovoltaic station in the Fergana region. Oman's Voltamp Energy SAOG will invest $350 million in the project. The plant is expected to generate 1 billion kWh of green electricity annually, saving 250 million cubic meters of natural gas.

item.title: Uzbekistan Holds Training on Practical Measures to Reduce Statelessness
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs participated in a training session in Tashkent focused on preventing and reducing statelessness. Organized by the National Human Rights Center and UNHCR, the event aimed to enhance officers' knowledge of international standards and practical skills in identifying and protecting stateless individuals.

item.title: Kazakhstan Discusses Investment, Trade, and Transport with Eight European Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister held bilateral meetings with counterparts from Germany, Romania, Latvia, Estonia, Ukraine, France, Croatia, and Bulgaria. Discussions focused on economic development, enhancing transit-transport potential, and attracting European companies for infrastructure modernization. Particular attention was given to strengthening strategic partnership with Germany.

item.title: Kazakhstan Marks 35 Years of Independence and Economic Transformation
item.description: Kazakhstan celebrates 35 years of independence since December 16, 1991, highlighting significant economic growth and regional leadership. Despite initial post-Soviet challenges, reforms and foreign investment fueled expansion, particularly in the oil and gas sector. The nation has navigated global crises to become Central Asia's largest economy.

item.title: Taliban Envoy to Pakistan Discusses Regional Security with UK Representative
item.description: Sardar Ahmad Shakib, the Taliban envoy to Pakistan, met with Richard Lindsay, the UK's Special Representative for Afghanistan. They discussed Afghanistan-UK relations, regional security developments, and the importance of continued diplomatic engagement for stability. The Taliban envoy stated the meeting was constructive.

item.title: Guterres: Climate Crisis Accelerating, Urges Stepped-Up Protection Efforts
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated that extreme weather events are claiming lives and reversing development gains due to the accelerating climate crisis. He urged increased efforts to protect people, emphasizing preventive measures and timely information on natural hazards.

item.title: Deutsche Bank Documents Reveal Links to Trump, Epstein, and Russian Oligarchs
item.description: Over 15 million internal Deutsche Bank documents have been leaked, exposing connections to Russian oligarchs, Donald Trump, and Jeffrey Epstein. The bank may have processed $582 million in suspicious transactions related to Epstein and inadvertently disclosed Trump's tax documents. Bank shares fell over 6% following the leak.

item.title: The Economist Predicts 10 Key Global Trends for 2027
item.description: The Economist has identified 10 major trends shaping global politics, economy, and technology in 2027. Forecasts include increased pressure on global markets, rising military risks in certain regions, and record-breaking weather warming. These trends are expected to define the global landscape.

item.title: Chevrolet's market share in Uzbekistan falls, BYD's grows significantly
item.description: Car sales in Uzbekistan decreased by 6.5% in the first ten months of the year compared to 2025. While Chevrolet's share dropped by 7.8%, BYD saw its sales increase. Tashkent remains the largest market, accounting for 29% of sales.

item.title: Uzbekistan Grants Citizenship to Over 91,000 People in Ten Years
item.description: Since 2016, Uzbekistan has granted citizenship to over 91,000 individuals, a significant increase compared to the 482 people who became citizens in the previous 24 years of independence. This information was provided by the National Center for Human Rights.

item.title: Kazakhstan Develops First Draft Law Using Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Kazakhstan has developed its first draft law using the AI-Quryltai platform, which possesses legal reasoning capabilities. The platform analyzed extensive data, public appeals, and international practices to create the draft law on 'Digital and Information Security of Children'.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Sign Strategic Partnership Agreement and Over 30 Other Documents
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman signed a strategic partnership agreement and over 30 other documents covering various sectors including industry, finance, customs, transport, and education. The agreements were exchanged following talks between Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Omani Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said in Muscat.

item.title: Uzbekistan Accredits Representative Offices of French and South Korean Banks
item.description: Uzbekistan has accredited representative offices of French bank Societe Generale and South Korean bank Hana Bank. These offices aim to study the country's financial market and expand cooperation with state bodies and financial organizations.

item.title: HRW: ICC Ruling Jeopardizes Justice for Afghan War Crimes Victims
item.description: Human Rights Watch warns that the International Criminal Court's decision to close part of its Afghanistan investigation may hinder accountability for alleged war crimes by U.S. and former Afghan government forces. The ruling affects alleged crimes committed before the Taliban's August 2021 takeover.

item.title: Euro Hits New 12-Month Low Against Kyrgyz Som; Other Currencies Mixed
item.description: The Euro fell for the fifth consecutive day, reaching a new 12-month low of 96.2114 Kyrgyz soms. The US Dollar remained stable, the Russian Ruble declined, while the Chinese Yuan and Kazakh Tenge strengthened against the som on November 18. The Euro has lost 2.19% in five days.

item.title: Tashkent Man Suspected of Sexual Assault Against Young Daughters
item.description: A man in Tashkent is under arrest on suspicion of sexually assaulting his daughters, aged 12 and 5. The National Social Protection Agency is involved. The family has been offered psychological and legal aid.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Send Over 20 Companies to Hungary for New Contracts
item.description: Kazakhstan's trade with Hungary has grown, with exports increasing by 56% in the first nine months of 2026. Over 20 Kazakh companies will attend a business forum in Debrecen to secure new contracts and attract investment.

item.title: SCO Member States Discuss Global Governance in Beijing
item.description: Representatives from Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states convened in Beijing for a roundtable on global governance. Discussions focused on practical experiences in maintaining regional stability and promoting shared values.

item.title: Kazakhstan Marks 35 Years of Independence and Economic Development
item.description: Kazakhstan celebrates 35 years of independence, marking a period of significant transformation and economic growth since December 16, 1991. Despite initial post-Soviet challenges, the country implemented reforms, introduced the tenge, and established the National Fund in 2000. It has since become Central Asia's largest economy, navigating global crises and modernizing its infrastructure.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reviews Solar Panel Usage and Investment Attractiveness
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate committee held public hearings on the effective use of solar panels and enhancing the sector's investment appeal. Monitoring across 13 regions revealed most panels function correctly but identified systemic issues like grid connection delays and inadequate financial incentives. Recommendations were made to address these problems and improve service.

item.title: Developer in Kyzyl-Kiya fined 200,000 soms for construction work acceptance violations
item.description: A construction company in Kyzyl-Kiya, 'Kyzyl-Kiya Kurulush', has been fined 200,000 soms for violating the procedure for accepting construction work stages. Violations were discovered during an inspection of a six-story residential building construction. The company failed to properly document acceptance of specific construction stages.

item.title: Uzbek women leaders study European public administration experience in Netherlands and Belgium
item.description: A group of potential women leaders from Uzbekistan are participating in an international internship in the Netherlands and Belgium to study European public administration. The program aims to develop leadership potential, negotiation skills, and strategic decision-making abilities. Participants are engaging in practical training and discussions on women's leadership in governance.

item.title: Mother's Home CEO Discusses International Expansion of Kazakh Charity
item.description: Kazakhstan's Mother's Home, a charity supporting women with children, has expanded internationally with 14 centers in five countries, helping around 500 children since 2023. CEO Timur Tuleuzhanov discussed adapting the project for other countries, its financing, and potential expansion into Azerbaijan and Tajikistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Accountability for Delayed Parliamentary Inquiries
item.description: Uzbekistan is developing legislation to hold officials accountable for failing to respond to parliamentary and senatorial inquiries within the stipulated deadlines. Data shows a significant number of inquiries are answered late or not at all, with responses often signed by lower-level staff. The proposed law will allow parliamentary bodies to seek administrative penalties or refer cases to the Prosecutor General's Office.

item.title: UN Allocates $18 Million for Winter Aid to Over 824,000 Vulnerable Afghans
item.description: The United Nations has allocated $18 million through the Central Emergency Response Fund to assist over 824,000 vulnerable individuals in Afghanistan as winter approaches. This funding will support seven projects focused on food security, healthcare, and shelter, aiming to prevent deaths amid worsening economic hardship and food insecurity. Priority will be given to returning migrants and displaced families.

item.title: Turkey Must Lead in Strengthening Regional Connectivity, Says Foreign Minister Fidan
item.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated that Turkey should take a leading role in enhancing regional connectivity due to its strategic position linking Europe, the Black Sea, the Caucasus, and Central Asia. Speaking after a security and connectivity meeting in Brussels, Fidan emphasized the need for practical steps beyond strategy development to foster cooperation in trade, energy, and data flow.

item.title: Less Than 10% of Pediatric Bone Marrow Transplants Needed in Uzbekistan Are Performed
item.description: Uzbekistan performs fewer than 10% of the annual bone marrow transplantations required for children, according to the Ministry of Health. In the first ten months of 2026, only 36 such procedures were conducted, far below the estimated annual need of at least 400. The ministry highlighted that many operations are performed abroad or at specialized centers within the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Discuss Parliamentary Oversight and Strengthen Ties
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber convened to discuss draft laws and parliamentary oversight. Speaker N. Ismailov highlighted the significance of the recent state visit to Oman for strengthening political dialogue and economic ties. The visit included meetings with Omani business leaders and the awarding of Uzbekistan's President with Oman's highest state honor, the Order of Al Said.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Integrate One-Year School Preparation into General Education System
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber is considering a bill to integrate one-year mandatory school preparation into the general education system. This initiative aims to provide legislative guarantees for children's access to this preparatory stage, which can be undertaken in preschools or schools, aligning national standards with international practices.

item.title: Taliban Report Over 500 People Returned to Afghanistan Yesterday Through Various Crossings
item.description: The Taliban announced that 537 people in 127 families returned to Afghanistan yesterday via multiple border crossings. Hamdullah Fitrat, deputy spokesperson, stated that significant numbers arrived through Torkham, Spin Boldak, Nimroz, and Islam Qala. Many returnees face economic hardship, unemployment, and lack of access to essential services.
